Maintenance Report — MNT-0076-009

Asset: WELL-0076 (SW-24 Well 076, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: separator Work started: 26 May 2024 08:00 · Finished: 05 Jun 2024 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 243 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Kevin Price, Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0076-0083 on 2024-05-23 Report written: 06 Jun 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the separator was overfilling and the dump valve was not opening. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0076-0083 showed the wellhead at 33.8 °C with the air at 30.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The level controller had failed. The well stayed shut in for about 8 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Paraffin build-up stopped the float from moving.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Isolated and depressurised the separator.
  2. Replaced the level controller.
  3. Calibrated the controller and tested the dump valve.

Summary of the fix: replaced level controller.

Testing and return to service

Cycled the separator three times; level control worked correctly. The well was returned to production.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0076-012

Asset: WELL-0076 (SW-24 Well 076, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 22 Sep 2024 08:00 · Finished: 16 Oct 2024 09:00 · Well stopped for this job: 577 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0076-0100 on 2024-09-19 Report written: 16 Oct 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the wellhead was cold and the pump jack was straining with a heavy, uneven load. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0076-0100 showed the wellhead at 33.6 °C with the air at 28.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 22 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

Consumables1,696

Total30,237

Compliance check

WS-07MetWritten the same day as the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Review sand control on this well.
  • Send the old pump for teardown.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0076-018

Asset: WELL-0076 (SW-24 Well 076, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 08 Aug 2025 08:00 · Finished: 09 Aug 2025 04:00 · Well stopped for this job: 20 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Megan Ward · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0076-0144 on 2025-08-07 Report written: 10 Aug 2025

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0076-0144 at 09:45 on 2025-08-07 found crude oil on the pad: about 5.3% of the pad area, estimated 1.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 3.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 1% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 265 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 212 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0076-018 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.81% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Absorbents and berms583

Total5,219

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).
